title: Hammerhead Claims - integration sprint notes
content:
Context:
Quick notes from kickoff + follow-ups with Hammerhead Insurance (claims team). They want a low-latency assistant to triage incoming claims, extract structured fields, and surface confidence scores for human review. Primary constraint: PHI-like PII handling and strict network controls (customer-managed VPC + KMS).

Attendees (2025-02-05 call):
- Jamie Ortega (Hammerhead, Claims Lead)
- Priya Nair (Hammerhead, Platform)
- Tom Becker (Hammerhead, Security)
- Aisha Patel (Redwood, Solutions Eng)
- Connor Liu (Redwood, SRE)

Call summary / goals:
- Pilot: 3-week sprint to validate ingestion, extraction, and human-in-the-loop workflows for Auto-Accident claims (subset of PII-limited fields).
- SLOs: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for single-turn extraction queries; throughput target 40 reqs/sec for burst windows.
- Data posture: traffic must stay inside Hammerhead VPC; logs with sensitive fields redacted before leaving customer boundary.
- Model: prefer open model family they can self-host (quantized Llama-2 style candidate); Redwood to propose verified model variants with latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Rollout plan: start with Dedicated nodes in Redwood private tenant -> mirror to Hammerhead private deployment if security gating demands.

Technical requirements captured:
- Network: bidirectional rules for control-plane in/out must be minimal; support for TLS mutual auth and customer-owned certs.
- Storage: KV cache must be optional and stored in customer-managed object store when possible.
- KMS: integrate with Hammerhead AWS KMS (customer key) for at-rest model/secret encryption.
- Audit: all inference calls must emit trace IDs and per-token cost metrics; Hammerhead will ingest traces into Splunk (they asked for example schema).
- Data retention: keep raw request content in customer vault for 30 days; redact PII after 7 days unless flagged for review.

Gotchas and red flags (from call):
- Their platform uses nonstandard chunking of multipart claim documents; parsing step must expose stable doc IDs and offsets so model can reference original text ranges.
- They expect deterministic outputs for extraction fields for adjudication logs — need prompt templates + post-processing rules to normalize dates, currency, and location fields.
- They flagged concern about tokenization mismatches across quantized runtimes; need exact token counts estimate per input to set cost/timeout limits.
- Streaming vs batch: Hammerhead wants near-instant single-record extraction (streaming token-by-token not required), but also periodic bulk reprocessing (batch). Must support both paths and consistent outputs.

Preliminary solution proposals (next sprint):
1) Ingest pipeline:
   - Lightweight preprocessor (in Python) to normalize claim PDF->text, assign stable doc offsets, label candidate PII spans.
   - Produce a short context snippet + field extraction prompt.
2) Model/cartography:
   - Redwood to run perf bench for 3 model variants (small / medium quantized / medium float) using Hammerhead sample corpus (anonymized). Show latency & token-cost.
3) Deployment options:
   - Option A: Redwood Dedicated w/ VPC peering (fastest) for pilot.
   - Option B: Private deployment in Hammerhead VPC (if security sign-off) — longer lead time.
4) Observability:
   - Per-request trace IDs; token-level cost in Redwood Console; Splunk ingestion hook.

Action items (owners + due):
- Aisha: Prepare perf matrix across three model variants using Hammerhead sample set; include token counts and 95p latency. Due 2025-02-10. (JIRA: JIRA-CLM-847)
- Connor: Draft network checklist for mTLS + VPC peering requirements; include firewall rules and egress controls. Due 2025-02-08.
- Priya (Hammerhead): Provide anonymized sample corpus (50 typical claims) and example adjudication rules (mapping table for normalized fields). Due 2025-02-07.
- Tom (Hammerhead security): Confirm KMS workflow for key rotation and confirm if HSM required. Due 2025-02-11.
- Marta: Prototype preprocessor script (text offsets + basic PII labeling) and attach to git PR for review. Due 2025-02-14.

Open questions / decisions to resolve:
- Determinism: Do we require exact deterministic generation (same output every time) or is high-confidence + normalization acceptable? Impact: need sampling temperature=0 vs small ensemble.
- KV cache retention: customer wants short term cache for speed but security wants minimal persistence. Need to agree TTL semantics and encryption-at-rest.
- Splunk schema: Hammerhead asked for an example ingestion payload (fields + sizes). Provide a sample JSON event.

Quick notes / prompt sketch (for extraction):
---PROMPT START---
You are an extraction assistant. Given the following canonical claim text (marked with offsets) extract the fields: incident_date (YYYY-MM-DD), insured_name (Last, First), claim_amount_usd (integer), incident_location (City, State), police_report_number (alphanumeric). Return JSON only. Normalize dates and currency. If field not present, return null. Include confidence score 0-1 for each field.
---INPUT (offsets)---
[0:512] <claim_text_here>
---PROMPT END---

Risks to call out in internal notes:
- If we recommend quantized medium models for cost reasons, we must proactively test hallucination risk on extraction fields (false positives inside long boilerplate).
- Model drift: periodic re-eval on adjudication set required; plan baseline eval harness now.

Possible tickets to create after perf run:
- "CLM-parse-offsets" -> preprocessor improvements
- "CLM-model-bench-2025-02" -> bench results + recommendation
- "CLM-observability-splunk-schema" -> Splunk ingestion hook and sample payload

References & links (placeholders asked on call):
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CLM/pages/3921 (team doc stub)
- Jira epic: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/JIRA-CLM-847

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep early demo narrow: 6 fields max, single claim per request. Avoid multi-turn for pilot.
- Emphasize clear failure modes in UI (highlight low-confidence fields and show source text offsets).
- Watch out for tokenization surprises when switching runtimes; include token-delta test in bench harness.

End of jot.
